This 12-week strength programme is designed for a 28-year-old female recreational lifter with no injuries and full gym access. It utilizes a **4-day Upper/Lower split**, which is highly effective for balancing recovery and training frequency. 

The programme is structured using **Block Periodization**, divided into three distinct 4-week phases:
1. **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy & Base Building** (Building muscle mass, work capacity, and movement proficiency).
2. **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Accumulation** (Transitioning to heavier loads and lower rep ranges).
3. **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Max Strength & Peaking** (Realizing strength gains and testing new personal bests).

We will use **RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion)** on a scale of 1–10 to manage auto-regulation, ensuring she doesn't burn out.

---

### The Weekly Split
*   **Monday:** Day 1 – Lower Body (Squat Focus)
*   **Tuesday:** Day 2 – Upper Body (Bench Focus)
*   **Wednesday:** Active Recovery / Rest
*   **Thursday:** Day 3 – Lower Body (Deadlift Focus)
*   **Friday:** Day 4 – Upper Body (Overhead Press Focus)
*   **Saturday & Sunday:** Rest / Active Recovery

---

### Phase 1: Hypertrophy & Base Building (Weeks 1–4)
The goal of this phase is to build a solid foundation of muscle tissue, improve work capacity, and perfect lifting mechanics under moderate fatigue.

#### **The Weekly Template (Phase 1)**

**Day 1: Lower Body (Squat Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Back Squat:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7-8
*   **B1. Romanian Deadlift (RDL):** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 7
*   **C1. Bulgarian Split Squat:** 3 sets x 10 reps/leg @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Hanging Knee Raises:** 3 sets x 12-15 reps

**Day 2: Upper Body (Bench Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7-8
*   **B1. Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip):** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Dumbbell Single-Arm Row:** 3 sets x 10 reps/arm @ RPE 8
*   **D1. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 15 reps

**Day 3: Lower Body (Deadlift Focus)**
*   **A1. Conventional Deadlift:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 7-8
*   **B1. Leg Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Lying Leg Curl:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Standing Calf Raises:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **D1. RKC Plank:** 3 sets x 30-45 second holds

**Day 4: Upper Body (Overhead Focus)**
*   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7-8
*   **B1. Pull-Ups (Assisted if needed) or Neutral Grip Cable Row:** 3 sets x 8-10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 3 sets x 12-15 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curls:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C3. Overhead Cable Tricep Extensions:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8

---

#### **Week-by-Week Progression (Phase 1)**

*   **Week 1 (Intro):** Keep RPE strictly at 7. Focus on establishing baseline weights. The last 2-3 reps of every set should feel comfortable but controlled.
*   **Week 2 (Load Progression):** Add 2.5kg to 5kg (5-10 lbs) to the main compound lifts (Squat, Bench, Deadlift, OHP). Target RPE 7.5 to 8.
*   **Week 3 (Overreach):** Push the intensity. Add another small increment of weight. Target RPE 8 to 8.5. This is the hardest week of the block.
*   **Week 4 (Deload & Pivot):** Reduce the volume to shed fatigue. Perform only **2 sets** per exercise instead of 3, and drop the weight by 10-15% (RPE 6). Do not skip this; it prepares her nervous system for Phase 2.

---

### Phase 2: Strength Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)
We now transition from hypertrophy to strength. Rep ranges drop, weights increase, and rest times between main lifts should increase to 2–3 minutes.

#### **The Weekly Template (Phase 2)**

**Day 1: Lower Body (Squat Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Back Squat:** 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8
*   **B1. Romanian Deadlift (RDL):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Leg Press (Narrow Stance):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Ab Wheel Rollouts:** 3 sets x 10 reps

**Day 2: Upper Body (Bench Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8
*   **B1. Weighted Pull-Ups or Heavy Lat Pulldown:** 4 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Dumbbell Flat Bench Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Barbell Pendlay Row:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **D1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 3 sets x 10-12 reps

**Day 3: Lower Body (Deadlift Focus)**
*   **A1. Conventional Deadlift:** 4 sets x 4 reps @ RPE 8
*   **B1. Barbell Hip Thrusts:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Goblet Cossack Squats:** 3 sets x 8 reps/leg @ RPE 7
*   **C2. Hanging Leg Raises:** 3 sets x 10 reps

**Day 4: Upper Body (Overhead Focus)**
*   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8
*   **B1. Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Dumbbell Incline Flyes:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Hammer Curls:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C3. Dual Rope Tricep Pushdowns:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8

---

#### **Week-by-Week Progression (Phase 2)**

*   **Week 5 (Transition):** Introduce the heavier 5-rep and 4-rep targets. Keep RPE at a solid 8 (leaving 2 reps in reserve on every set).
*   **Week 6 (Load Progression):** Increase weight on all main lifts by 2.5kg (5 lbs). Target RPE 8.5.
*   **Week 7 (Peak Intensity):** Increase weight again. Target RPE 9 (only 1 rep left in reserve on the final sets).
*   **Week 8 (Deload):** Reduce sets to 2 per exercise. Drop intensity on all lifts by 15%. This allows her joints and central nervous system (CNS) to recover before the high-intensity peaking phase.

---

### Phase 3: Max Strength & Peaking (Weeks 9–12)
This phase is designed to maximize neurological adaptation (recruiting more muscle fibers) and prepare her to test her strength limits in Week 12.

#### **The Weekly Template (Phase 3)**

**Day 1: Lower Body (Squat Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Back Squat:** 4 sets x 3 reps @ RPE 8.5–9
*   **B1. Romanian Deadlift (RDL):** 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Bulgarian Split Squat (Bodyweight or light DBs):** 2 sets x 8 reps/leg (focus on stability)
*   **C2. Pallof Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps/side

**Day 2: Upper Body (Bench Focus)**
*   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 4 sets x 3 reps @ RPE 8.5–9
*   **B1. Chest-Supported T-Bar Row:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 12 reps

**Day 3: Lower Body (Deadlift Focus)**
*   **A1. Conventional Deadlift:** 3 sets x 2 reps @ RPE 8.5–9
*   **B1. Barbell Hip Thrusts:** 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8.5
*   **C1. Lying Leg Curl:** 2 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **C2. Plank with Shoulder Taps:** 3 sets x 20 total taps

**Day 4: Upper Body (Overhead Focus)**
*   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 4 sets x 3 reps @ RPE 8.5–9
*   **B1. Pull-Ups (Bodyweight or assisted):** 3 sets x Max Reps (stop 2 reps short of failure)
*   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 3 sets x 10 reps
*   **C2. Dumbbell Hammer Curls:** 2 sets x 10 reps

---

#### **Week-by-Week Progression (Phase 3)**

*   **Week 9 (Heavy Triples):** Establish heavy triples (3 reps) for Squat, Bench, and OHP, and a heavy double (2 reps) for Deadlift. Target RPE 8.5.
*   **Week 10 (Peak Load):** Increase weight to a true RPE 9-9.5. This will be the heaviest weight she handles before testing.
*   **Week 11 (Taper Week):** 
    *   *Reduce volume drastically to shed fatigue.*
    *   Perform only **2 sets of 2 reps** on main lifts at a light RPE 7.
    *   Cut accessory work down to 1-2 light sets.
    *   No training past Wednesday/Thursday to ensure full recovery for Week 12.
*   **Week 12 (Test Week):**
    *   **Monday (Squat & Bench Test):** Warm up thoroughly. Build up to a heavy single (1RM) or a heavy double (2RM) depending on her comfort level. 
        *   *Example Squat Attempt Selection:* Warm-ups -> Opener (a weight she can easily do for 3 reps) -> 2nd Attempt (a small PR or match of old PR) -> 3rd Attempt (New PR attempt if 2nd felt good).
    *   **Wednesday (Deadlift & OHP Test):** Follow the same testing protocol for Deadlift and Overhead Press.
    *   **Friday:** Light, fun pump session (high reps, low intensity) to celebrate the end of the cycle.

To integrate conditioning without compromising her strength gains (avoiding the "interference effect"), we will add **two conditioning sessions per week** that target different energy systems:

1.  **Session 1: Aerobic Capacity / Active Recovery (Low Intensity - LISS).** Best performed on **Wednesday** (mid-week rest day) to promote blood flow and recovery.
2.  **Session 2: Anaerobic Power / Metabolic Conditioning (High Intensity - HIIT/Metcon).** Best performed on **Saturday** (weekend) or immediately after **Friday's Upper Body session** so she has Sunday for full recovery before squatting on Monday.

Here is how the conditioning progresses across the 12 weeks, matching the physiological demands of each phase.

---

### Phase 1: Hypertrophy & Base Building (Weeks 1–4)
*The goal here is to build an aerobic base and increase work capacity to help her recover faster between strength sets.*

#### **Session 1: Aerobic Base (LISS)**
*   **When:** Wednesday (Active Recovery)
*   **Modality:** Incline Treadmill Walk, Stairmaster, or Stationary Bike.
*   **Protocol:** 30–40 minutes of continuous steady-state cardio.
*   **Intensity:** Zone 2 (RPE 5-6 / Heart Rate 120–140 BPM). She should be able to maintain a conversation comfortably.

#### **Session 2: Aerobic Intervals (Rowing or Echo/Airdyne Bike)**
*   **When:** Saturday (or Friday post-workout)
*   **Protocol:** 
    *   5-minute warm-up.
    *   **Intervals:** 10 rounds of:
        *   60 seconds moderate-high effort (RPE 7-8)
        *   60 seconds active recovery (very light pedalling/rowing)
    *   5-minute cool-down.
*   **Total Time:** 30 minutes.

---

### Phase 2: Strength Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)
*As the lifting weights get heavier, we transition her high-intensity conditioning to low-impact, explosive movements (sleds and kettlebells) to protect her joints while boosting metabolic conditioning.*

#### **Session 1: Aerobic Base (LISS) + Core**
*   **When:** Wednesday (Active Recovery)
*   **Protocol:** 30 minutes of Zone 2 cardio (Incline treadmill walk or Elliptical).
*   **Finisher:** 3 rounds of:
    *   60-second Plank
    *   15 Bird-Dogs per side
    *   15 Glute Bridges

#### **Session 2: Sled & Kettlebell Metcon**
*   **When:** Saturday (or Friday post-workout)
*   **Protocol:** 15-Minute EMOM (Every Minute on the Minute):
    *   **Minute 1:** 15 Kettlebell Swings (moderate weight)
    *   **Minute 2:** 50-meter Sled Push (moderate load) or 15 Wall Balls
    *   **Minute 3:** 45 seconds of Row/Echo Bike (moderate pace)
    *   *Repeat for 5 total rounds.*
*   **Intensity:** RPE 8. This will spike her heart rate but has zero eccentric loading, meaning minimal muscle soreness (DOMS) for Monday's squats.

---

### Phase 3: Max Strength & Peaking (Weeks 9–12)
*During this phase, central nervous system (CNS) fatigue is high. Conditioning is scaled back to preserve energy for her heavy lifts and ensure she peaks perfectly in Week 12.*

#### **Session 1: Pure Recovery LISS**
*   **When:** Wednesday
*   **Protocol:** 20–30 minutes of very light walking or outdoor cycling. 
*   **Intensity:** RPE 4-5 (Keep heart rate under 120 BPM). The goal is strictly blood flow and mental decompression.

#### **Session 2: Alactic Power Intervals (Echo Bike or Rower)**
*   **When:** Saturday (Weeks 9 & 10 only. **Skip in Week 11 & 12** to allow full taper).
*   **Protocol:** Short, explosive sprints with full recovery to keep the CNS sharp without generating metabolic fatigue.
    *   **Intervals:** 6 to 8 rounds of:
        *   10 seconds maximal effort sprint (RPE 9-10)
        *   50 seconds complete rest (passive recovery)
*   **Total Time:** 10-15 minutes (including warm-up).

---

### Summary of the Weekly Schedule (Phases 1 & 2)
*   **Monday:** Day 1 – Lower Body (Squat Focus)
*   **Tuesday:** Day 2 – Upper Body (Bench Focus)
*   **Wednesday:** **Conditioning Session 1 (LISS / Active Recovery)**
*   **Thursday:** Day 3 – Lower Body (Deadlift Focus)
*   **Friday:** Day 4 – Upper Body (OHP Focus)
*   **Saturday:** **Conditioning Session 2 (HIIT / Metcon)**
*   **Sunday:** Full Rest / Stretch

### 1. The Golden Rules of the Rehab Hinge
Before she touches a bar, establish these three rules with her:
*   **The 24-Hour Rule:** She should feel zero pain during the movement. If she experiences any tightness or dull ache *the next day* that exceeds a 2/10 on a pain scale, the volume or load was too high. We hold the weight/volume constant for the next week.
*   **Tempo is Non-Negotiable:** All hinges in Weeks 7–9 must use a **3-0-1-0 tempo** (3-second eccentric/lowering, 0-second pause at the bottom, 1-second concentric/concentric, 0-second pause at the top). This prevents her from using momentum or "jerking" the weight, which is when re-tears occur.
*   **No Training to Failure:** Every set must finish with at least 3–4 reps left in the tank (RPE 6–7).

---

### 2. The Step-by-Step Hinge Progression (Weeks 7–12)

We will measure **Total Hinge Reps** per week to ensure we don't spike her workload too quickly.

```
Week 7:  30 reps (RPE 5-6)  |  Partial ROM (RDL to mid-thigh)
Week 8:  24 reps (RPE 6-7)  |  Increased ROM (RDL to knee)
Week 9:  18 reps (RPE 7)    |  Floor/Block Pull (Reduced reps, increased load)
Week 10: 15 reps (RPE 7.5)  |  Block Pull (Strength focus)
Week 11: 4 reps  (RPE 6)    |  Taper (Deload)
Week 12: 5 reps  (RPE 8-9)  |  Test (5RM Block Pull)
```

#### **Week 7: Re-Patterning & High Reps (Low Load)**
*   **Movement:** Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
*   **ROM:** Partial. Lower the bar only to **mid-thigh/just above the kneecap**. Do not let the hips drop too low.
*   **Volume/Intensity:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 5–6 (Total: 30 reps)
*   **Goal:** Increase blood flow and test the hamstring's tolerance to light, repetitive stretching.

#### **Week 8: Increasing ROM (Moderate Load)**
*   **Movement:** Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
*   **ROM:** Full RDL. Lower the bar to **just below the kneecap/mid-shin** (only as deep as a pain-free stretch allows).
*   **Volume/Intensity:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6–7 (Total: 24 reps)
*   **Goal:** Safely load the hamstring in a slightly deeper stretched position.

#### **Week 9: Transition to Pulling (Low Reps, Higher Load)**
*   **Movement:** Trap Bar Deadlift (High Handles) OR Conventional Deadlift from 2-inch blocks.
*   **ROM:** Pulling from an elevated position. This eliminates the deepest part of the hinge (off the floor) while allowing her to practice "pulling" rather than just "lowering."
*   **Volume/Intensity:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 7 (Total: 18 reps)
*   **Goal:** Re-introduce concentric drive and heavier bracing.

*   **ROM:** Elevated pull.
*   **Volume/Intensity:** 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 7.5–8 (Total: 15 reps)
*   **Goal:** Build confidence handling heavier loads (around 75-80% of her pre-injury capacity).

*   **Movement:** Conventional Deadlift from 2-inch blocks.
*   **Volume/Intensity:** 2 sets x 2 reps @ RPE 6 (Total: 4 reps)
*   **Goal:** Keep the movement pattern fresh while shedding all residual fatigue before test week.

*   **Movement:** Conventional Deadlift from 2-inch blocks.
*   **Volume/Intensity:** Build up to a strong, pain-free **5-Rep Max** (RPE 8–9).
*   **Goal:** Establish a safe, heavy baseline to kickstart her next training block.

### 3. Trainer's Decision Tree (What to do if she feels pain)

If she reports tightness or pain (above a 2/10) during a session:
1.  **Step 1: Reduce the ROM.** If RDLs below the knee hurt, limit them to mid-thigh.
2.  **Step 2: Reduce the Load.** Drop the weight by 20%. If pain persists, stop the movement.
3.  **Step 3: Regress to Isometrics.** If any dynamic hinging hurts, swap the exercise to **3 sets of 30-second Single-Leg Glute Bridges (holding the top position)**. Isometrics have an analgesic (pain-relieving) effect on healing tendons and muscles.

This is the complete, finalized 12-week training programme. It has been fully updated to reflect her initial goals (posterior-chain and deadlift focus), the mid-programme hamstring strain at the end of Week 2, her highly successful rehab phase, and her transition into an upper-body specialization block to keep her motivated and progressing.

---

### The Master Schedule Overview
*   **Weeks 1–2:** 4-Day Upper/Lower Split (Posterior Chain & Deadlift Focus)
*   **Weeks 3–6:** 4-Day Split: 3 Upper / 1 Lower (Hamstring Rehab & Upper-Body Hypertrophy Specialization)
*   **Weeks 7–9:** 4-Day Split: 3 Upper / 1 Lower (Progressive Hinge Re-Introduction & Upper-Body Strength)
*   **Weeks 10–12:** 4-Day Split: 3 Upper / 1 Lower (Upper-Body 1RM Peaking & Deadlift 5RM Block Test)

---

### Phase 1: Base Building & The Pivot (Weeks 1–4)

#### **Week 1 & Week 2: Posterior-Chain Base Building**
*The goal is to build structural volume in the hamstrings, glutes, and upper back.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Lower Body (Squat & Posterior Volume)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Back Squat:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7 (W1), RPE 8 (W2)
    *   **B1. Romanian Deadlift (RDL):** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 7 (Focus on deep hinge and hamstring stretch)
    *   **C1. Barbell Hip Thrusts:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8 (1-second squeeze at top)
    *   **C2. Hanging Knee Raises:** 3 sets x 12-15 reps
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Upper Body (Bench & Upper Back)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7 (W1), RPE 8 (W2)
    *   **B1. Barbell Pendlay Row:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip):** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **D1. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   30–40 mins Incline Treadmill Walk (Zone 2 / RPE 5-6).
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Lower Body (Deadlift Focus - Volume)**
    *   **A1. Conventional Deadlift:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 7 (W1), RPE 8 (W2) *(Note: Injury occurs at the end of this session in Week 2)*
    *   **B1. Deficit Deadlift (standing on a 1-2 inch plate):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7
    *   **C1. Lying Leg Curl:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Standing Calf Raises:** 3 sets x 15 reps
    *   **D1. RKC Plank:** 3 sets x 30-45 second holds
*   **Friday: Day 4 – Upper Body (OHP & Lats)**
    *   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7 (W1), RPE 8 (W2)
    *   **B1. Neutral Grip Cable Row:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 3 sets x 12-15 reps
    *   **C2. Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curls:** 3 sets x 12 reps
    *   **C3. Overhead Cable Tricep Extensions:** 3 sets x 12 reps
*   **Saturday: Conditioning Session 2 (Aerobic Intervals)**
    *   Rowing Machine: 5-min warm-up. 10 rounds of: 60s moderate-high effort (RPE 7-8) / 60s light recovery. 5-min cool-down.

---

#### **Week 3 & Week 4: Pivot to Upper-Body Specialization & Quad/Core Rehab**
*The hamstring strain has occurred. We pivot to a 3-Day Upper / 1-Day Lower split. We completely remove the hip hinge and hamstring loading. Week 4 is a scheduled deload to allow systemic healing.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Upper Body (Bench Focus - Modified)**
    *   **A1. Feet-Up Barbell Bench Press:** 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 7.5 (W3), 2 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6 (W4 Deload) *(Feet on bench to eliminate hamstring bracing)*
    *   **B1. Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row:** 4 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8 (W3), 2 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6 (W4 Deload)
    *   **C1. Incline Dumbbell Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip):** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **D1. Cable Tricep Pushdowns:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Lower Body (Quad Strength & Rehab)**
    *   **A1. Leg Press (Low & Narrow Foot Placement):** 4 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 7.5 (W3), 2 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 6 (W4 Deload)
    *   **B1. Heel-Elevated Dumbbell Goblet Squat:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 7 (Keep torso upright, stop just shy of parallel)
    *   **C1. Standing Calf Raises:** 3 sets x 15 reps (Slow 3-second eccentric)
    *   **C2. RKC Plank:** 3 sets x 30-45 second holds
    *   **D1. Physio Rehab:** Pain-free bodyweight mobility and light glute activation.
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   20–30 mins Upper-Body Ergometer (SkiErg or Arm Crank) OR very light stationary cycling (low resistance, high cadence) if completely pain-free.
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Upper Body (OHP & Shoulders)**
    *   **A1. Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press:** 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8 (W3), 2 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 6 (W4 Deload)
    *   **B1. Neutral Grip Cable Row:** 4 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 4 sets x 12-15 reps @ RPE 8.5
    *   **C2. Rear Delt Flyes (Pec Dec or Dumbbell):** 3 sets x 15 reps
    *   **D1. Dumbbell Hammer Curls:** 3 sets x 12 reps
*   **Friday: Day 4 – Upper Body (Pull-Up & Arm Hypertrophy)**
    *   **A1. Assisted or Bodyweight Pull-Ups:** 4 sets x Max Reps (Stop 2 reps short of failure)
    *   **B1. Incline Dumbbell Bench Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Barbell Bicep Curls:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Overhead Cable Tricep Extensions:** 3 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **D1. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 20 reps
*   **Saturday: Conditioning Session 2 (Upper-Body/Core Metcon)**
    *   4 rounds of: 30s Battle Ropes, 30s Russian Twists, 30s Seated Dumbbell Press (light), 90s rest.

---

### Phase 2: Upper-Body Strength & Progressive Hinge Re-Entry (Weeks 5–9)

#### **Week 5 & Week 6: Upper-Body Strength & Quad Overload**
*We transition her upper-body lifts to heavy strength work (5-rep ranges). Lower body remains strictly quad/core/rehab focused (no hinging yet).*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Upper Body (Heavy Bench)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press (Feet-Up):** 5 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8 (W5), RPE 8.5 (W6)
    *   **B1. Heavy Chest-Supported T-Bar Row:** 4 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Flat Bench Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Lat Pulldown (Close Grip):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Lower Body (Quad Strength & Rehab)**
    *   **A1. Leg Press (Low & Narrow):** 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **B1. Heel-Elevated Dumbbell Goblet Squat:** 3 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 8 (Heavy)
    *   **C1. Seated Calf Raises:** 3 sets x 15 reps
    *   **C2. Hanging Leg Raises:** 3 sets x 10 reps
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   30 mins flat outdoor walking or light stationary cycling.
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Upper Body (Heavy OHP)**
    *   **A1. Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press:** 5 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8 (W5), RPE 8.5 (W6)
    *   **B1. Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip):** 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 4 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 9
    *   **C2. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **Friday: Day 4 – Upper Body (Weighted Pull-Ups & Arms)**
    *   **A1. Weighted Pull-Ups (or Lat Pulldown):** 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8 (W5), RPE 8.5 (W6)
    *   **B1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Hammer Curls:** 3 sets x 10 reps
    *   **C2. Dual Rope Tricep Pushdowns:** 3 sets x 10 reps
*   **Saturday: Conditioning Session 2 (Low-Impact Metcon)**
    *   15-Minute EMOM: Min 1: 45s SkiErg or Battle Ropes | Min 2: 15 Bodyweight Squats | Min 3: 45s Plank hold.

---

#### **Weeks 7–9: Progressive Hinge Integration**
*Physio has cleared her for moderate hip-hinges. We implement the 3-week progressive ramp-up on Day 2, while continuing to push her upper-body strength.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Upper Body (Heavy Bench)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 5 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8.5 (Feet flat on floor, normal leg drive)
    *   **B1. Heavy Chest-Supported T-Bar Row:** 4 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Flat Bench Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Lat Pulldown (Close Grip):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Lower Body (The Hinge Ramp-Up)**
    *   **A1. Leg Press (Low & Narrow):** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **B1. Hinge Progression (Choose week):**
        *   **Week 7:** Barbell RDL (Partial ROM to mid-thigh, 3-0-1-0 tempo): 3 sets x 10 reps @ **RPE 5–6 Max**
        *   **Week 8:** Barbell RDL (Full ROM to below knee, 3-0-1-0 tempo): 3 sets x 8 reps @ **RPE 6–7 Max**
        *   **Week 9:** Conventional Deadlift from 2-inch blocks: 3 sets x 6 reps @ **RPE 7 Max**
    *   **C1. Bodyweight Glute Bridges:** 3 sets x 15 reps (2-second squeeze at top)
    *   **C2. Hanging Leg Raises:** 3 sets x 10 reps
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   30 mins flat outdoor walking or light stationary cycling.
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Upper Body (Heavy OHP)**
    *   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 5 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8.5
    *   **B1. Seated Cable Row (Wide Grip):** 4 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 4 sets x 10 reps @ RPE 9
    *   **C2. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **Friday: Day 4 – Upper Body (Weighted Pull-Ups & Arms)**
    *   **A1. Weighted Pull-Ups (or Lat Pulldown):** 4 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 8.5
    *   **B1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C1. Hammer Curls:** 3 sets x 10 reps
    *   **C2. Dual Rope Tricep Pushdowns:** 3 sets x 10 reps
*   **Saturday: Conditioning Session 2 (Low-Impact Metcon)**
    *   15-Minute EMOM: Min 1: 10 Light Kettlebell Deadlifts (perfect hinge focus) | Min 2: 45s SkiErg or Battle Ropes | Min 3: 45s Plank hold.

---

### Phase 3: Upper-Body Peak & Deadlift Consolidation (Weeks 10–12)

#### **Week 10: Strength Consolidation**
*We transition her to a slightly heavier, but highly controlled, deadlift variation from blocks. We prepare her upper body for true 1RM testing.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Upper Body (Bench Peak Prep)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 4 sets x 3 reps @ RPE 9
    *   **B1. Chest-Supported Row:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8.5
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Incline Press:** 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 8
    *   **C2. Face Pulls:** 3 sets x 12 reps
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Lower Body (Deadlift Strength Capacity)**
    *   **A1. Conventional Deadlift (from 2-inch blocks):** 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 7.5–8
    *   **B1. Barbell Hip Thrusts:** 3 sets x 8 reps @ RPE 8 (Heavy glute loading, minimal hamstring stretch)
    *   **C1. Lying Leg Curl:** 2 sets x 12 reps @ RPE 7 (Light, controlled)
    *   **C2. Plank with Shoulder Taps:** 3 sets x 20 total taps
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   20–30 mins light walking (Recovery).
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Upper Body (OHP Peak Prep)**
    *   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 4 sets x 3 reps @ RPE 9
    *   **B1. Pull-Ups (Bodyweight):** 3 sets x Max Reps
    *   **C1. Dumbbell Lateral Raises:** 3 sets x 10 reps
    *   **C2. Dumbbell Hammer Curls:** 2 sets x 10 reps
*   **Friday: Day 4 – Upper Body (Pump & Grip - Fun Session)**
    *   **A1. Dumbbell Flat Bench Press:** 3 sets x 10 reps
    *   **B1. Lat Pulldown:** 3 sets x 10 reps
    *   **C1. Cable Bicep Curls superset with Tricep Overhead Extensions:** 3 sets x 12 reps each
    *   **D1. Farmer's Walks (Heavy):** 3 sets x 30 meters (Grip and core focus)
*   **Saturday: Conditioning Session 2 (Light Intervals)**
    *   Stationary Bike: 15 mins (30s moderate / 30s easy).

---

#### **Week 11: Taper Week**
*We cut all accessory work in half and drop volume drastically to shed fatigue before testing.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Upper Body (Bench Taper)**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** 2 sets x 2 reps @ RPE 7
    *   **B1. Chest-Supported Row:** 2 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 6
*   **Tuesday: Day 2 – Lower Body (Deadlift Taper)**
    *   **A1. Conventional Deadlift (from 2-inch blocks):** 2 sets x 2 reps @ RPE 6
    *   **B1. Bodyweight Glute Bridges:** 2 sets x 10 reps
*   **Wednesday: Conditioning Session 1 (LISS)**
    *   20 mins very light walking.
*   **Thursday: Day 3 – Upper Body (OHP Taper)**
    *   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** 2 sets x 2 reps @ RPE 7
    *   **B1. Pull-Ups (Bodyweight):** 2 light sets
*   **Friday & Saturday:** Rest (No training or conditioning to ensure full recovery).

---

#### **Week 12: The Test Week**
*We celebrate her upper-body progress by testing her 1RMs, while establishing a safe, strong baseline for her return to deadlifting.*

*   **Monday: Day 1 – Bench Press 1RM Test**
    *   **A1. Barbell Bench Press:** Warm up, then build to a new lifetime **1RM**.
    *   **B1. Leg Extensions:** 3 sets x 15 reps (Light pump)
    *   **C1. Standing Calf Raises:** 3 sets x 15 reps
*   **Wednesday: Day 2 – OHP 1RM & Deadlift Capacity Test**
    *   **A1. Standing Overhead Barbell Press (OHP):** Warm up, then build to a new **1RM**.
    *   **B1. Conventional Deadlift (from 2-inch blocks):** Warm up, then build to a strong, pain-free **5-Rep Max (5RM)**. *(Capped at RPE 8.5 to protect the healed hamstring).*
*   **Friday: Day 3 – Celebratory Pump Session**
    *   Light, full-body pump session (high reps, low intensity) to celebrate the end of the cycle.
